newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Nine young bikers killed in southern Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Nine young bikers killed in southern Vietnam.

text.p: Nine young Vietnamese motorcycle racers died after a high-speed crash in the southern resort and port of Vung Tau, a senior police officer said on Tuesday.
The accident happened on Saturday night when a truck driver braked to avoid five of the motorcycles racing towards him, shedding his container load of fish in their path.
Seven of the riders died on impact and two others died in hospital, the officer said.
"A couple of weeks ago we stopped a race with about 20 to 30 motorbikes," he said. "I call this a social evil which has been caused by the market mechanism."
High-speed racing has become a common expression of rebellion among the communist country's increasingly affluent urban youth.

Suggested solutions to the problem have included fining offenders, expelling them from schools and colleges, impounding their bikes and setting up a legal racecourse in Ho Chi Minh City, where races are common.
Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet is also reported to have suggested tougher restrictions on the import of fast motorbikes.
There are now some two million motorbikes in Vietnam -- a country of 75 million people -- about half of which are in Ho Chi Minh City, formerly Saigon.
